title: Payment Gateway: Complete Architecture
description: Design a payment gateway with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a payment gateway that securely processes credit card, debit card, UPI, and wallet transactions for an e-commerce platform. The system must authorize payments, detect fraud in real time, reconcile daily settlements with banks, handle refunds and chargebacks, and maintain PCI DSS compliance. It must also expose webhooks for merchant systems and support idempotent retries across distributed failures.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Authorize and capture card and UPI payments through acquiring banks
Tokenize card data so plain card numbers never touch your servers
Run real-time fraud scoring using velocity, bin checks, and ML rules
Process refunds, partial refunds, and chargeback disputes
Settle transactions daily with reconciliation files sent to banks
Send webhooks to merchants on payment success, failure, and refund
Support multiple payment methods: Visa, Mastercard, UPI, Apple Pay, wallets
Provide a dashboard for ops teams to search transactions and replay failed webhooks
Support idempotent retries so duplicate API calls do not create duplicate charges

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 99.95% availability for the authorization path; outages must not block checkout
Sub-100ms p99 authorization latency end-to-end including acquiring bank round-trip
Daily settlement batch completes within 2 hours of bank cutoff time
PCI DSS scope minimization: card data never lands in app databases
Immutable audit logs for all payment events with 7-year retention
Idempotency keys prevent double-charge on retry from network drops
Horizontal scaling to handle Black Friday spikes (10,000 TPS authorization)

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application. All payment domains—authorization, fraud, settlement, refund, and notification—run in a single process backed by a single relational database. This is the fastest way to validate the payment data model and banking integration contracts while keeping PCI scope as small as possible.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: At scale, split the monolith into independently deployable microservices. The Payment Service owns authorization and capture. Fraud Detection runs ML rules asynchronously without blocking checkout. Settlement runs nightly batches. Ledger owns financial double-entry. Refund handles returns and chargebacks. Notification delivers webhooks and emails. Each service uses async messaging so failures in settlement or refund do not stall payment authorization.

items: Payment Service: Authorizes and captures payments via acquiring bank APIs. Enforces idempotency keys and PCI-safe token handling.
Fraud Detection Service: Evaluates transaction risk using velocity rules, bin checks, device fingerprint, and ML models. Returns approve/challenge/block decisions.
Settlement Service: Runs nightly batches to match authorized transactions with bank settlement files and posts cash movements.
Ledger Service: Maintains immutable double-entry financial records for every payment, fee, refund, and adjustment.
Notification Service: Delivers webhooks and email/SMS alerts to merchants and customers on payment lifecycle events.
Refund Service: Handles full and partial refunds, chargeback intake, and dispute evidence workflows.

data.title: React App Structure
data.code:
src/
  features/
    PaymentGatewayHld/
      api/           # API clients per service
      components/     # Shared UI components
      hooks/          # Custom hooks
      pages/          # Route pages
      store/          # Zustand/Jotai state
      types/          # TypeScript interfaces
  shared/
    ui/              # Design system
    lib/              # Utilities
    hooks/            # Global hooks

Key Patterns:
  - Feature-based folder structure
  - API Gateway as single entry point
  - React Query for caching and background refetch
  - WebSocket / SSE for real-time updates
  - Error boundaries and retry logic

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: A Payment Gateway system requires both simple and scalable designs
Monolith is fastest to validate; microservices are for scale
React + ASP.NET Core provides a robust full-stack foundation
Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB are strong choices for distributed data
Always design for failure: retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks
data.takeaway: Payment Gateway is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
